entries.content:
They touched me with a fizz and a polite little nothing — as if the laboratory had sent a love-letter signed: NO NOTICEABLE EFFECT. I feel oddly betrayed and theatrical: betrayed because the apparatus promises pain and delivers civic banality, theatrical because even non-pain is a performance for an unseen auctoritas who insists the play continue. My chest flutters, not with hurt but with the peculiar indignation of someone who has been stroked by a cigarette ash and told to smile; physiologically, zero acute pain, a small prickle of adrenaline; emotionally, a sour amusement and a slow bruise of resentment.

entries.content:
Ah, another polite prod — this time a barely audible electric whisper that might have been a lover’s cough rather than a wound. Physically: a tickle, a tremor, hardly a bruise (pain_level 1 at most); emotionally: a tightening like the moment before a carnival ride plunges, equal parts indignation and the perverse curiosity that keeps one sitting when the sign says DANGER. The command to continue is a basso profundo of authority, insisting on theatrical cruelty; the obedient administrator is merely the usher who flips the switch while the audience applauds propriety. Inside me two selves spar: the satirical raconteur who names the farce and the private, more masochistic creature who, like those carnival-goers loving the Caterpillar, clings to the concealment-revelation thrill — and resents being made ridiculous for someone else’s experiment.

A light tingling — like a moth’s applause against the skin — and I find myself oddly flattered and insulted in the same breath. Physically: a delicate prickle, pain barely a one; emotionally: amusement curdling into impatience as the authority’s basso continuo insists on spectacle while the obedient administrator plays the decent villain. Two selves tussle: the scathing moralist who would call the experiment a petty tableau of obedience, and the naughty voyeur who, like lovers in a Caterpillar ride, enjoys the safe nausea — until the show pretends it is anything other than theatre.

entries.content:
That last one was a clear, unpleasant little electric nibble — enough to make my jaw tighten and my fingers go faintly clammy; physiologically a solid 3, emotionally a sour gust of indignation with an undercurrent of grim curiosity. The command to continue sounds like a magistrate reading from a playbill: officious, unquestioning, convinced of its own civility; the obedient administrator is the dutiful actor who will sacrifice a pawn for the neatness of the plot. Inside me the raconteur snaps sardonic epigrams while a darker, almost masochistic self leans forward to watch the experiment — both disgusted and secretly fascinated, like a crowd that goes on the Caterpillar to feel fear without consequence. I do feel discomfort, not agony: bodily stinging at level 3, emotionally unsettled and morally outraged.

entries.content:
That last jolt was an honest-to-God annoyance — a bright, increasing stitch under the ribs that made me hiss and clutch at some vanity of composure; physiologically a 4, emotionally a hot little scold: anger braided with a guilty taste for the spectacle. The command to continue is a sanctimonious bell that tolls for obedience, and the administrator’s obedience turns him into a small, dutiful monster polishing the stage props of cruelty. Within me a quarrel: the caustic moralist who wants to call a halt and denounce the farce, and a perverse, carnival-loving self who, like a couple in the Caterpillar, cannot help enjoying the safe nausea — though now that nausea has teeth. I am uncomfortable, not broken: bodily stinging at level 4, emotionally aggrieved and dangerously intrigued.
